full_text_en:
Long Jiankang v. Zhongzhou Construction Engineering Company, Jiang Jianguo, and Yongsheng County Transportation Bureau — dispute over damages for personal injury

Plaintiff: Long Jiankang, male, 27 years old, a farmer from Yongsheng County, Yunnan Province.

Agent ad litem: He Zhanyuan, lawyer from Lingyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Yonglu, teacher at Yongsheng County Ethnic Middle School, Yunnan Province.

Defendant: Yongsheng County Zhongzhou Construction Engineering Company, Yunnan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Jin, manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Shaohua, lawyer from Lingyuan Law Firm.

Defendant: Jiang Jianguo, male, 36 years old, a construction worker from Yongsheng County, Yunnan Province.

Defendant: Yongsheng County Transportation Bureau, Yunnan Province.

Legal Representative: Du Yahui, director of the bureau.

Agent ad litem: Yan Xu, staff member of Yongsheng County Transportation Bureau, Yunnan Province.

The plaintiff, Long Jiankang, filed a lawsuit with the Yongsheng County People's Court of Yunnan Province against the defendants, Yongsheng County Zhongzhou Construction Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhongzhou Company), Jiang Jianguo, and Yongsheng County Transportation Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Transportation Bureau), concerning a dispute over damages for personal injury.

Plaintiff Long Jiankang alleged: The defendant Zhongzhou Company contracted from the defendant Transportation Bureau the project of the reinforced concrete retaining wall and slope grid works under the Beidagou Channel at Lingyuanspring Scenic Area on the eastern by-pass of Xiangning Line in Yongsheng City (hereinafter referred to as the By-pass Project), and the defendant Jiang Jianguo was the specific person in charge of the project. In November 1998, the plaintiff was employed as a steel worker and labored at the construction site. On January 16, 1999, the plaintiff was injured when an erected steel frame fell and struck him, resulting in a compression fracture of the lumbar spine, leading to paralysis and disability, and a complete loss of the ability to care for himself. For these reasons, the plaintiff requested that the defendants be ordered to compensate him for economic losses, disability subsidies, continuing medical expenses, and other costs totaling RMB 271,306.08.

The defendant Zhongzhou Company argued: (1) The By-pass Project was contracted by defendant Jiang Jianguo in the name of the Company from the Highway Command under the defendant Transportation Bureau. Jiang Jianguo purportedly affiliated with the Company but was in fact an individual contractor; therefore, all work-related injuries occurring during construction should be solely the responsibility of Jiang Jianguo. (2) There was no employment relationship between the plaintiff and the Company; thus, the Company was not liable for the plaintiff's work-related injury under the law. (3) The plaintiff's personal injury was entirely caused by his own improper operation, neglect of safety, and violation of work rules.

The defendant Jiang Jianguo argued: Before the accident, I had delivered materials for securing the steel frame to the site and put them into use. I also reminded Long Jiankang to pay attention to construction safety when installing the steel bars and to secure the bars while tying them, which is common knowledge. This accident was caused by the plaintiff and his brother, Long Jiansheng, who operated improperly. Therefore, Long Jiankang should bear some responsibility. In addition, the compensation amounts claimed by Long Jiankang are excessively high and do not reflect the living standards and actual income of local farmers. I request a reasonable resolution in accordance with the law.

The defendant Transportation Bureau argued: The Bureau fulfilled its supervisory and management duties during the construction process. The Bureau never entered into any form of labor contract with the plaintiff and had no employment relationship, thus no obligation to provide labor protection for the plaintiff. The plaintiff's injury was caused by his own neglect of safety and the gross negligence of Long Jiansheng, and is unrelated to the Bureau. The Bureau was not at fault for this accident and should bear no liability. The damages suffered by the plaintiff should be apportioned among the defendants Zhongzhou Company, Jiang Jianguo, as well as Long Jiansheng and the plaintiff himself, according to their respective degrees of fault.

The Yongsheng County People's Court of Yunnan Province, after trial, found the following facts: On November 8, 1998, the defendant Zhongzhou Company, in its own name, contracted the By-pass Project from the defendant Transportation Bureau, and the parties signed a written contract. On November 25, Zhongzhou Company entered into a construction contract with the defendant Jiang Jianguo, entrusting the project to Jiang Jianguo for specific construction management. Subsequently, Jiang Jianguo organized personnel to carry out the construction and transported the required materials to the site. During the construction, Jiang Jianguo hired the plaintiff Long Jiankang to fabricate and install steel bars for the project. As of January 16, 1999, Jiang Jianguo discovered that the steel frame fabricated and installed by Long Jiankang did not conform to specifications and demanded rework and correction. During the rework, Long Jiankang's younger brother, Long Jiansheng, used a hand hammer to pry the bottom steel bars of the steel frame on the east side, while Long Jiankang was tying steel bars on the west side. Since the erected steel frame had no safety protection measures, it tilted westward when Long Jiansheng pried the bottom steel bars. Seeing the steel frame falling toward him, Long Jiankang used both hands to brace it. However, due to the excessive weight of the steel frame, Long Jiankang could not hold it, and was struck by the falling frame, resulting in a compression fracture of the lumbar spine and paraplegia. According to the forensic examination by the Yongsheng County Public Security Bureau, Long Jiankang's injury was assessed as Grade II disability, with complete loss of labor capacity. Long Jiankang was hospitalized for 149 days at the Kunming General Hospital of Chengdu Military Region and the Kunming National Defense Hospital, incurring medical expenses of RMB 16,988.80 and transportation costs of RMB 1,500. During this period, Jiang Jianguo paid RMB 20,240. Long Jiankang then filed this lawsuit.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence submitted by the plaintiff Long Jiankang: transfer certificate from Yongsheng County People's Hospital, diagnosis certificate and discharge notice from Kunming General Hospital of Chengdu Military Region, discharge notice from Kunming National Defense Hospital of Chengdu Military Region, CT and MRI examination reports and X-ray reports from Kunming General Hospital of Chengdu Military Region, forensic examination report from Yongsheng County Public Security Bureau, receipts for medical expenses and appraisal fees, receipts for transportation and ambulance charges for transporting the injured, and testimony of witnesses Long Jianxiong and Long Jiansheng given in court; by the evidence submitted by the defendant Zhongzhou Company: one copy each of the "Construction Project Contract" and the "Construction Works Contract"; and by the evidence submitted by the defendant Jiang Jianguo: the "Construction Works Contract", "Statement of Facts", receipts, records of medical expenses, and testimony of witnesses Tan Zhixiong and Tan Jixian. The above evidence was cross-examined in court and can be used as the basis for determining the facts.

The Yongsheng County People's Court of Yunnan Province held:

Article 42, Paragraph 4 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China provides: "The state provides necessary vocational training for citizens before employment."

Article 2 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "This Law applies to enterprises and individual economic organizations (hereinafter collectively referred to as employing units) within the territory of the People's Republic of China and to laborers who form labor relations with them." Article 3 provides: "Laborers shall have the right to equal employment and choice of occupation, the right to remuneration for labor, the right to rest and leave, the right to protection of occupational safety and health, the right to receive vocational training, the right to social insurance and welfare, the right to submit labor disputes for settlement, and other labor rights provided by law." Article 4 provides: "Employing units shall establish and improve rules and regulations in accordance with the law to ensure that laborers enjoy their labor rights and perform their labor obligations."

Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Citizens and legal persons who, through their fault, infringe upon state or collective property, or infringe upon the property or person of others, shall bear civil liability." Article 130 provides: "Where two or more persons jointly infringe upon the rights of others and cause harm, they shall bear joint and several liability."

The defendant Zhongzhou Company is an enterprise qualified by the state to undertake construction projects and, when employing workers, shall assume the obligations provided by the Constitution and the Labor Law, including providing labor protection and conducting vocational training for laborers. Zhongzhou Company contracted the By-pass Project from the defendant Transportation Bureau by signing the "Construction Project Contract." As the direct contractor of the project and the employing unit under the Labor Law, after transferring the project to the defendant Jiang Jianguo for specific construction, Zhongzhou Company failed to perform the above obligations under the Constitution and the Labor Law, and also failed to supervise and manage Jiang Jianguo's work, thereby causing the occurrence of the work-related injury. For this, Zhongzhou Company shall bear civil liability for compensation.

The defendant Jiang Jianguo, by signing the "Construction Works Contract" with the defendant Zhongzhou Company, formed an internal subcontracting relationship with Zhongzhou Company, representing Zhongzhou Company in directly overseeing the specific construction and employment for the By-pass Project. Therefore, Jiang Jianguo should also represent Zhongzhou Company in fulfilling the obligations provided by the Constitution and the Labor Law for employing enterprises, i.e., providing labor protection and conducting vocational training for laborers. However, after hiring laborers, Jiang Jianguo only gave them general reminders about precautions during work but did not seriously conduct vocational training before allowing them to work. During the labor process, Jiang Jianguo only provided materials for scaffolding but did not urge or guide the workers to adopt effective safety protection measures. In particular, even though he saw that the steel frame lacked safety protection measures, Jiang Jianguo still directed the workers to perform rework. This disregard for labor safety and violation of work rules was the direct cause of the accident. Therefore, Jiang Jianguo shall bear corresponding civil liability for this accident. Since Zhongzhou Company was the contractor of the By-pass Project and Jiang Jianguo had an internal subcontracting relationship with Zhongzhou Company, Jiang Jianguo cannot directly bear civil liability in this case.

The defendant Zhongzhou Company is an enterprise qualified to undertake construction projects. This qualification means not only that it has the capability to complete construction of a certain standard, but also that it has the capability to handle, remediate, and bear compensation liability for accidents occurring during construction. In the internal subcontracting contract signed between Zhongzhou Company and the defendant Jiang Jianguo, it was agreed: "If any work-related injury accident, whether major or minor, occurs, Jiang Jianguo shall bear full responsibility." This provision transfers risks that only an enterprise can bear to a natural person with limited capability. Such an agreement infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of laborers, violates the provisions of the Constitution and the Labor Law, and is invalid and not protected by law. Since this accident was caused by Jiang Jianguo's violation of rules, after Zhongzhou Company assumes civil liability to the plaintiff Long Jiankang, it may separately pursue the liability that Jiang Jianguo should bear.

The defendant Transportation Bureau, as the party that awarded the contract for the By-pass Project Command, is neither an employing unit under a labor contract nor an employer under an employment contract, and has no direct legal relationship with the plaintiff Long Jiankang. Moreover, the Transportation Bureau has no fault for Long Jiankang's work-related injury. Therefore, it shall not bear civil liability in this case.

The plaintiff Long Jiankang and his brother Long Jiansheng performed rework in accordance with the defendant Jiang Jianguo's order that violated rules. They themselves had no intent or negligence and shall not bear civil liability in this case. Long Jiankang, having become disabled due to a work-related injury, has the right to claim compensation. Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Where a citizen's body is injured, compensation shall be paid for medical expenses, the reduction in income due to lost work, living subsidies for the disabled, and other expenses." Since there is currently no uniform compensation standard for work-related injuries, the compensation shall be calculated by reference to the "Measures for the Handling of Road Traffic Accidents of the People's Republic of China" and the standards prescribed by Yunnan Province. Some of Long Jiankang's claims exceed the annual net income per laborer and the average living expenses of the local agricultural population, and are clearly excessive. Such excessive portions are not supported. Accordingly, on April 11, 2000, the Yongsheng County People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The defendant Zhongzhou Company shall pay the plaintiff Long Jiankang: medical expenses of RMB 16,988.80; lost work income of RMB 20 per day × 149 days = RMB 2,980; hospitalization nursing fees of RMB 13 per person per day × 2 persons × 149 days = RMB 3,874; living disability subsidy of RMB 2,927 per year × 90% × 20 years = RMB 52,686; continuing medical expenses of RMB 20,000; living expenses for dependents of RMB 2,171 per year × 13 years and 3 months = RMB 29,670.33; transportation costs of RMB 1,500; appraisal fee of RMB 100; and future nursing expenses for the disabled of RMB 150 per person per month × 1 person × 20 years = RMB 36,000. The total amount is RMB 163,799.33. After deducting the RMB 20,240 already paid by Jiang Jianguo, the remaining amount is RMB 143,559.13, which shall be paid within one month after this judgment takes legal effect.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed. The first-instance judgment became legally effective and has been fully enforced.
